name: DefineHumanPlayerGeneral

retail.definition: Binary Ninja reports an x87-confused prototype (arg1..arg8 @ st0..st7, int32_t arg9, float arg10 @ 0xc); the observed stack use is a first argument that receives a six-dword result block (rep movsd, ecx=6, at 0x004101AD) and a context pointer read as [esp+0x34] at 0x00410075 and passed to the 0x004B8A50 getter.
retail.registrar: Registered at 0x0041001B through registrar 0x004B8890 as 'DefineHumanPlayerGeneral' with argc bounds (0, -1); it has no static callers and is invoked from the script VM.

retail.behavior: For each script argument index the getter 0x004B8A50 is called and the returned x87 value is scaled and stored: index 0 raw at 0x0056E1E8; indices 1-3 multiplied by 4096000.0f and by 9.259259e-06f; indices 4-5 multiplied by 4096.0; index 6 multiplied by 30.0 and converted to an integer; index 7 raw; index 0 is also stored at 0x0056E208; then table A (17 entries, stride 0x10) and table B (stride 0x10 until 0x00538C18) are filled with unscaled getter values. The function copies a six-dword result block into its first stack argument and returns.
retail.tool_evidence: Binary Ninja MCP bn_function_info, bn_function_callees, bn_function_disassembly, bn_function_decompile and bn_memory_read on retail igi.exe at 0x00410070, 0x004B8A50 and the scale constants.

candidate_source.signature: void __cdecl DefineHumanPlayerGeneral(void* qvm_context, const float* arguments, unsigned int argument_count)

findings: The candidate takes a flat float array and an explicit count; retail takes no array. Every retail argument is fetched individually through the script accessor 0x004B8A50, which the candidate never calls.
The candidate scales only the odd array elements by human_player_scale_inverse (1/108000) alone; retail multiplies indices 1-3 by 4096000.0f and then by 9.259259e-06f in 80-bit x87 arithmetic.
The candidate's wide-scale long double is computed and then discarded ((void)wide), so the 4096000.0 factor never reaches any stored value.

The candidate writes three scaled fields and a first field; retail writes eight named values (0x0056E1E8..0x0056E204), a second copy of index 0 at 0x0056E208, then two tables of unscaled getter values.
Retail converts index 6 to an integer with fistp after multiplying by 30.0; the candidate has no equivalent.
Retail returns a six-dword result block through its first stack argument; the candidate returns void.

The candidate's header comment claims this is a complete port; the record's semantic review claims 'the candidate reads the retail data as it is stored; it performs no float arithmetic', which is false for this function.
